```text
1	# 43_copilot_proxy.sh - GitHub Copilot -> Anthropic/OpenAI proxy for Claude Code
2	#   (shared bash + zsh).
3	#
4	# Runs the maintained copilot-api fork (caozhiyuan/copilot-api, npm
5	# @jeffreycao/copilot-api) so a GitHub Copilot subscription can back Claude Code
6	# (and any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible client). The original ericc-ch/copilot-api
7	# is unmaintained (its issue #233 points at the fork) but still works via
8	# COPILOT_API_PKG=copilot-api@0.7.0 — flags differ per package, see
9	# _copilot_pkg_flavor. Both packages share the same token file, so switching
10	# needs no re-auth. Full guide + risks: docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md.
11	#
12	# Public surface:
13	#   copilot-proxy [start|stop|status|restart|logs|whoami|auth]   - manage the proxy
14	#   copilot-run <cmd...>       - run any command with the proxy env injected
15	#                                (auto-starts the proxy first)
16	#   claude-copilot [args...]   - one-off Claude Code session on the proxy
17	#                                (specstory-wrapped when available; zero file writes)
18	#   copilot-here [on|off|status] - sticky per-project toggle via the gitignored
19	#                                ./.claude/settings.local.json (never touches the
20	#                                committed .claude/settings.json)
21	#   copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c] - switch the pinned model (edits settings.local.json
22	#                                when copilot-here is on, else the global state file)
23	#
24	# Settings-layer design (why settings.local.json / env vars, and NOT the
25	# committed .claude/settings.json nor ~/.claude/settings.json):
26	#   - ~/.claude/settings.json is chezmoi-managed (dot_claude/modify_settings.json)
27	#     and would make the proxy always-on for every project.
28	#   - ./.claude/settings.json is committed (claude-plans-here puts plansDirectory
29	#     there) — proxy config must not leak into git.
30	#   - Claude Code precedence (low→high): user < project < settings.local.json
31	#     (gitignored) < CLI flags. GOTCHA (verified 2026-07): current Claude Code
32	#     lets the settings.local.json env block BEAT inherited shell env vars —
33	#     so copilot-run/claude-copilot cannot override a project where
34	#     `copilot-here on` points elsewhere (run `copilot-here off` first).
35	#
36	# Portability notes (POSIX subset, both shells source this file):
37	#   - runs the proxy via `bunx` (matches 07_bunx_cli.sh); pinned version avoids a
38	#     per-launch @latest registry round-trip. Override with COPILOT_API_PKG.
39	#   - no ZLE/compdef/setopt/glob-qualifiers here (bash would error on source).
40	#
41	# Env (set in ~/.shellrc.adhoc or ~/.config/{zsh/secrets.zsh,bash/secrets.sh}):
42	#   COPILOT_PROXY_PORT   default: 4141        - port the proxy listens on
43	#   COPILOT_API_PKG      default: @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14
44	#                                             - bunx package spec (pin/upgrade;
45	#                                               copilot-api@0.7.0 = old original)
46	#   COPILOT_PROXY_RATE   default: 15          - --rate-limit seconds; ONLY used
47	#                                               by the original package (the fork
48	#                                               has no rate limiter)
49	#   COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET  default: 0           - 1 = inject extra quota-saving env
50	#                                               (fewer background calls, but a
51	#                                               slightly degraded Claude Code UX)
52	
53	# --- shared constants / helpers -------------------------------------------------
54	
55	_copilot_port() { printf '%s' "${COPILOT_PROXY_PORT:-4141}"; }
56	_copilot_pkg()  { printf '%s' "${COPILOT_API_PKG:-@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14}"; }
57	
58	# CLI flavor from the package spec: the ORIGINAL bare `copilot-api` takes
59	# --rate-limit/--wait and has `check-usage`; the fork (and anything else)
60	# doesn't. Strips a trailing @version, but not the @scope/ prefix.
61	_copilot_pkg_flavor() {
62	  local name; name="$(_copilot_pkg)"
63	  case "$name" in
64	    copilot-api|copilot-api@*) printf 'original' ;;
65	    *) printf 'fork' ;;
66	  esac
67	}
68	_copilot_base() { printf 'http://localhost:%s' "$(_copilot_port)"; }
69	_copilot_logfile() { printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-api-$(_copilot_port).log"; }
70	_copilot_pidfile() { printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-api-$(_copilot_port).pid"; }
71	
72	# Global default-model state file (used by copilot-run/claude-copilot when the
73	# project has no copilot-here pin). Written by `copilot-model`.
74	_copilot_model_state() {
75	  printf '%s' "${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/copilot-proxy/model"
76	}
77	
78	# Resolve the model for env injection: $COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL > state file > default.
79	#
80	# Model-id shape matters (verified 2026-07):
81	#   - HYPHENATED ids (claude-opus-4-8), not dotted (claude-opus-4.8): Claude
82	#     Code only recognizes hyphenated family names — dotted ids fall back to
83	#     a legacy "[Opus 4] retired" label AND a 200k context assumption.
84	#   - "[1m]" suffix: Copilot serves opus-4-8 / sonnet-5 with a 1M context
85	#     window; the suffix makes Claude Code strip it, send the context-1m
86	#     beta header, and size HUD/compaction to 1M (otherwise it assumes 200k
87	#     and shows >100% context). Claude Code-only: raw API clients must send
88	#     the plain id — the proxy rejects a literal "...[1m]" model.
89	_copilot_default_model() {
90	  if [ -n "${COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL:-}" ]; then
91	    printf '%s' "$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL"
92	  elif [ -f "$(_copilot_model_state)" ]; then
93	    command head -n 1 "$(_copilot_model_state)"
94	  else
95	    printf '%s' "claude-opus-4-8[1m]"
96	  fi
97	}
98	
99	# Is the proxy answering on its port?
100	_copilot_alive() {
101	  command curl -fsS --max-time 2 "$(_copilot_base)/v1/models" >/dev/null 2>&1
102	}
103	
104	# --- proxy manager --------------------------------------------------------------
105	
106	# Manage the copilot-api proxy. Subcommands: start|stop|status|restart|logs|auth.
107	# Example:
108	#   copilot-proxy start          # background-start on $COPILOT_PROXY_PORT
109	#   copilot-proxy status         # is it up? which models?
110	copilot-proxy() {
111	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
112	    emulate -L zsh
113	    setopt localoptions pipefail
114	  else
115	    set -o pipefail
116	  fi
117	
118	  if ! command -v bunx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
119	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: bunx not found (needs bun via mise)." >&2
120	    return 1
121	  fi
122	
123	  local port pkg logf pidf
124	  port="$(_copilot_port)"; pkg="$(_copilot_pkg)"
125	  logf="$(_copilot_logfile)"; pidf="$(_copilot_pidfile)"
126	
127	  local action="${1:-status}"
128	  case "$action" in
129	    start)
130	      if _copilot_alive; then
131	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: already running on port $port" >&2
132	        return 0
133	      fi
134	      # First run needs `copilot-proxy auth` to store a ghu_ token; warn if absent.
135	      if [ ! -f "$HOME/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token" ]; then
136	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not authenticated yet — run 'copilot-proxy auth' first." >&2
137	        return 1
138	      fi
139	      # Flag sets differ per package: only the original has --rate-limit/--wait
140	      # (the fork ships no rate limiter — mitigate with COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1).
141	      if [ "$(_copilot_pkg_flavor)" = "original" ]; then
142	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: starting ($pkg) on port $port (rate-limit ${COPILOT_PROXY_RATE:-15}s) ..."
143	        # nohup + background; detach so it survives the shell. Log to a file.
144	        nohup bunx "$pkg" start \
145	          --port "$port" \
146	          --rate-limit "${COPILOT_PROXY_RATE:-15}" \
147	          --wait \
148	          >"$logf" 2>&1 &
149	      else
150	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: starting ($pkg) on port $port ..."
151	        nohup bunx "$pkg" start \
152	          --port "$port" \
153	          >"$logf" 2>&1 &
154	      fi
155	      printf '%s\n' "$!" >"$pidf"
156	      # Wait up to ~20s for it to answer.
157	      local i=0
158	      while [ "$i" -lt 20 ]; do
159	        if _copilot_alive; then
160	          printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: up → $(_copilot_base)  (logs: copilot-proxy logs)"
161	          return 0
162	        fi
163	        sleep 1
164	        i=$((i + 1))
165	      done
166	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: did not come up in time — check 'copilot-proxy logs'." >&2
167	      return 1
168	      ;;
169	    stop)
170	      # Prefer the tracked pid; fall back to a broad match.
171	      if [ -f "$pidf" ]; then
172	        local pid; pid="$(cat "$pidf" 2>/dev/null)"
173	        [ -n "$pid" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null
174	        command rm -f -- "$pidf"
175	      fi
176	      command pkill -f "copilot-api.*--port $port" 2>/dev/null
177	      sleep 1
178	      if _copilot_alive; then
179	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: still answering on $port (another instance?)" >&2
180	        return 1
181	      fi
182	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: stopped (port $port free)"
183	      ;;
184	    restart)
185	      copilot-proxy stop
186	      copilot-proxy start
187	      ;;
188	    status)
189	      if _copilot_alive; then
190	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: RUNNING on $(_copilot_base)"
191	        printf '%s\n' "  models: $(command curl -fsS --max-time 3 "$(_copilot_base)/v1/models" 2>/dev/null \
192	          | command grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | command sed 's/"id":"//;s/"//' | command grep -i claude | command tr '\n' ' ')"
193	      else
194	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not running on port $port  (start: copilot-proxy start)"
195	        return 1
196	      fi
197	      ;;
198	    logs)
199	      if [ -f "$logf" ]; then command tail -n "${2:-40}" "$logf"; else
200	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: no log file at $logf" >&2; return 1; fi
201	      ;;
202	    auth)
203	      # One-time device login → stores a ghu_ token copilot-api can exchange.
204	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: launching copilot-api device login ..."
205	      bunx "$pkg" auth
206	      ;;
207	    whoami|usage)
208	      # Real login check: exchanges the stored token against GitHub and prints
209	      # the account / plan / quota. Fails loudly if the token is missing/expired.
210	      if [ ! -f "$HOME/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token" ]; then
211	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not authenticated — run 'copilot-proxy auth' first." >&2
212	        return 1
213	      fi
214	      if [ "$(_copilot_pkg_flavor)" = "original" ]; then
215	        bunx "$pkg" check-usage
216	      elif _copilot_alive; then
217	        # Fork has no check-usage subcommand; its /usage endpoint serves the
218	        # GitHub quota payload (same data as the bundled /usage-viewer).
219	        if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
220	          command curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$(_copilot_base)/usage" | jq '{
221	            plan: (.copilot_plan // .access_type_sku // "unknown"),
222	            quota_reset: (.quota_reset_date // null),
223	            quotas: ((.quota_snapshots // {}) | map_values(
224	              if type == "object" then
225	                {remaining, entitlement, percent_remaining, unlimited}
226	              else . end))
227	          }'
228	        else
229	          command curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$(_copilot_base)/usage"
230	        fi
231	      else
232	        # Proxy down → the fork's `debug` still validates auth state / paths.
233	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not running — showing auth/debug info instead of quota." >&2
234	        bunx "$pkg" debug
235	      fi
236	      ;;
237	    -h|--help|help)
238	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|logs [N]|whoami|auth]"
239	      ;;
240	    *)
241	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: unknown action '$action' (try --help)" >&2
242	      return 1
243	      ;;
244	  esac
245	}
246	
247	# --- session wrapper (Layer 1: one-off, zero file writes) ------------------------
248	
249	# Run any command with the copilot-proxy env injected (per-process only —
250	# nothing is written to disk). Auto-starts the proxy when it isn't answering.
251	# GOTCHA (verified 2026-07): current Claude Code lets the settings.local.json
252	# env block beat inherited shell env, so this does NOT win inside a project
253	# where `copilot-here on` pins something else — `copilot-here off` first.
254	# Example:
255	#   copilot-run claude                      # raw Claude Code on the proxy
256	#   copilot-run specstory run claude        # specstory-wrapped session
257	copilot-run() {
258	  if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
259	    printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-run <cmd> [args...]   (injects ANTHROPIC_* proxy env)" >&2
260	    return 1
261	  fi
262	  if ! _copilot_alive; then
263	    copilot-proxy start || return 1
264	  fi
265	  local model; model="$(_copilot_default_model)"
266	  # Opt-in quota savers (COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1): prepended as NAME=VALUE args
267	  # to `env`. Off by default — they degrade the Claude Code UX a little.
268	  if [ "${COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET:-0}" = "1" ]; then
269	    set -- \
270	      CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER="0" \
271	      CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION="false" \
272	      CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY="0" \
273	      DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS="1" \
274	      "$@"
275	  fi
276	  # `command env` (not bare var-prefix) so the vars are strictly per-process:
277	  # POSIX var-prefix on a *function* call would leak into the current shell.
278	  command env \
279	    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="$(_copilot_base)" \
280	    ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="dummy" \
281	    ANTHROPIC_MODEL="$model" \
282	    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="$model" \
283	    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="claude-sonnet-5[1m]" \
284	    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="claude-haiku-4-5" \
285	    ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL="claude-haiku-4-5" \
286	    CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC="1" \
287	    "$@"
288	}
289	
290	# One-off Claude Code session backed by the Copilot proxy. Nothing on disk
291	# changes — revert is just running plain `claude` next time.
292	# Wraps in `specstory run` when specstory is installed (markdown auto-save,
293	# same convention as scode/svibe); opt out with --no-specstory. Extra args go
294	# to the claude CLI (via specstory's -c "custom command" passthrough).
295	# Example:
296	#   claude-copilot                 # specstory run claude (proxy env)
297	#   claude-copilot -c              # continue last session
298	#   claude-copilot --no-specstory  # raw claude, no markdown auto-save
299	claude-copilot() {
300	  local ss="auto"
301	  case "${1:-}" in
302	    --no-specstory) ss="never"; shift ;;
303	    --specstory)    shift ;;
304	    -h|--help)
305	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
306	      printf '%s\n' "  One-off Claude Code session on the Copilot proxy (no file writes)."
307	      printf '%s\n' "  Sticky per-project instead: copilot-here on"
308	      return 0 ;;
309	  esac
310	  if [ "$ss" = "auto" ] && command -v specstory >/dev/null 2>&1; then
311	    if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
312	      copilot-run specstory run claude -c "claude $*"
313	    else
314	      copilot-run specstory run claude
315	    fi
316	  else
317	    copilot-run claude "$@"
318	  fi
319	}
320	
321	# --- per-project toggle (Layer 2: sticky, gitignored settings.local.json) --------
322	
323	# Env keys we own in .claude/settings.local.json (kept in one place so `off`
324	# removes exactly what `on` added — including the COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET extras,
325	# regardless of the knob's value at `off` time).
326	_copilot_here_keys='["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL","ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN","ANTHROPIC_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL","CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC","CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER","CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION","CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY","DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS"]'
327	
328	# Pin THIS project to the Copilot proxy via ./.claude/settings.local.json —
329	# the gitignored local layer that overrides the committed .claude/settings.json
330	# (so claude-plans-here's plansDirectory stays untouched). Plain `claude` then
331	# uses the proxy here until `copilot-here off`.
332	# Example:
333	#   copilot-here on        # pin project to the proxy
334	#   copilot-here status    # pinned? which model?
335	#   copilot-here off       # unpin (removes only our env keys)
336	copilot-here() {
337	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
338	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: jq is required" >&2; return 1
339	  fi
340	
341	  local settings=".claude/settings.local.json"
342	  local action="${1:-status}"
343	  case "$action" in
344	    on)
345	      command mkdir -p .claude
346	      local base='{}'
347	      [ -f "$settings" ] && base="$(command cat "$settings")"
348	      [ -n "$base" ] || base='{}'
349	      local model; model="$(_copilot_default_model)"
350	      local quiet="${COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET:-0}"
351	      local tmp; tmp="$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-here.XXXXXX")" || return 1
352	      if printf '%s' "$base" | jq \
353	          --arg base_url "$(_copilot_base)" --arg model "$model" --arg quiet "$quiet" '
354	          .env = ((.env // {}) + {
355	            ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: $base_url,
356	            ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: "dummy",
357	            ANTHROPIC_MODEL: $model,
358	            ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: $model,
359	            ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: "claude-sonnet-5[1m]",
360	            ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: "claude-haiku-4-5",
361	            ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL: "claude-haiku-4-5",
362	            CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: "1"
363	          } + (if $quiet == "1" then {
364	            CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER: "0",
365	            CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION: "false",
366	            CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY: "0",
367	            DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS: "1"
368	          } else {} end))' >"$tmp"; then
369	        command mv -- "$tmp" "$settings"
370	      else
371	        command rm -f -- "$tmp"
372	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: jq failed; $settings unchanged" >&2
373	        return 1
374	      fi
375	      # Claude Code only auto-gitignores settings.local.json when IT creates the
376	      # file — since we created it, belt-and-braces via .git/info/exclude.
377	      if command git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
378	        if ! command git check-ignore -q "$settings" 2>/dev/null; then
379	          local exclude; exclude="$(command git rev-parse --git-dir)/info/exclude"
380	          printf '%s\n' ".claude/settings.local.json" >>"$exclude"
381	        fi
382	      fi
383	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: ON — $settings pins Claude Code to $(_copilot_base) (model: $model)"
384	      printf '%s\n' "  plain \`claude\` in this project now uses the proxy (restart any running session)"
385	      _copilot_alive || printf '%s\n' "  ⚠ proxy not running — start it with: copilot-proxy start"
386	      ;;
387	    off)
388	      if [ ! -f "$settings" ]; then
389	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: already off (no $settings)"
390	        return 0
391	      fi
392	      local tmp; tmp="$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-here.XXXXXX")" || return 1
393	      # Remove only OUR env keys; drop .env when it empties; keep other content.
394	      if jq --argjson keys "$_copilot_here_keys" '
395	          .env = ((.env // {}) | with_entries(select(.key as $k | ($keys | index($k)) == null)))
396	          | if .env == {} then del(.env) else . end' \
397	          "$settings" >"$tmp"; then
398	        if [ "$(jq -r 'if . == {} then "empty" else "kept" end' "$tmp")" = "empty" ]; then
399	          command rm -f -- "$tmp" "$settings"
400	          printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: OFF — removed $settings (it held only proxy config)"
401	        else
402	          command mv -- "$tmp" "$settings"
403	          printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: OFF — proxy env removed from $settings (other content kept)"
404	        fi
405	        printf '%s\n' "  plain \`claude\` is back on the real Anthropic backend (restart any running session)"
406	      else
407	        command rm -f -- "$tmp"
408	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: jq failed; $settings unchanged" >&2
409	        return 1
410	      fi
411	      ;;
412	    status)
413	      if [ -f "$settings" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL // empty' "$settings" 2>/dev/null)" != "" ]; then
414	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: ON  (base: $(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL' "$settings"), model: $(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL // "(unset)"' "$settings"))"
415	        _copilot_alive || printf '%s\n' "  ⚠ proxy not running — start it with: copilot-proxy start"
416	      else
417	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: off  (enable: copilot-here on; one-off: claude-copilot)"
418	        return 1
419	      fi
420	      ;;
421	    -h|--help|help)
422	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-here [on|off|status]   (toggles ./.claude/settings.local.json)"
423	      ;;
424	    *)
425	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: unknown action '$action' (try --help)" >&2
426	      return 1
427	      ;;
428	  esac
429	}
430	
431	# --- model switcher -------------------------------------------------------------
432	
433	# Switch which Copilot model is pinned. Claude Code's own /model picker sends
434	# dated Anthropic ids the Copilot backend rejects (model_not_supported), so pin
435	# here. Use the HYPHENATED ids the proxy lists (claude-opus-4-8); an optional
436	# "[1m]" suffix tells Claude Code the model has a 1M context window (see
437	# _copilot_default_model) — it is stripped before validating against the proxy.
438	#
439	# Write target (never the committed .claude/settings.json):
440	#   - copilot-here is ON in this project → ./.claude/settings.local.json
441	#   - otherwise → global state file (~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/model), which
442	#     claude-copilot / copilot-run / the next `copilot-here on` pick up.
443	# Example:
444	#   copilot-model opus-4-8         # fuzzy → claude-opus-4-8 (opus-4.8 works too)
445	#   copilot-model 'opus-4-8[1m]'   # same + 1M-context hint for Claude Code
446	#   copilot-model -l               # list available (live from proxy)
447	#   copilot-model -c               # print current (+ where it came from)
448	copilot-model() {
449	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
450	    emulate -L zsh
451	    setopt localoptions pipefail
452	  else
453	    set -o pipefail
454	  fi
455	
456	  local settings=".claude/settings.local.json"
457	  local statef; statef="$(_copilot_model_state)"
458	
459	  # copilot-here mode? (local settings file carries our proxy env)
460	  local target="state"
461	  if [ -f "$settings" ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 \
462	     && [ "$(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL // empty' "$settings" 2>/dev/null)" != "" ]; then
463	    target="local"
464	  fi
465	
466	  # List available model ids (live proxy, else a static Claude fallback).
467	  _copilot_model_list() {
468	    local json
469	    if json="$(command curl -fsS --max-time 3 "$(_copilot_base)/v1/models" 2>/dev/null)"; then
470	      printf '%s\n' "$json" | command grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | command sed 's/"id":"//;s/"//' | command sort
471	    else
472	      printf '%s\n' \
473	        claude-opus-4-8 claude-opus-4-7 claude-opus-4-6 claude-opus-4-5 \
474	        claude-sonnet-5 claude-sonnet-4-6 claude-sonnet-4-5 claude-haiku-4-5
475	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: proxy not reachable — showing fallback list" >&2
476	    fi
477	  }
478	
479	  # Current pinned model, from whichever layer is active.
480	  _copilot_model_current() {
481	    if [ "$target" = "local" ]; then
482	      jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL // "(unset)"' "$settings"
483	    else
484	      _copilot_default_model
485	    fi
486	  }
487	
488	  local arg="${1:-}"
489	  case "$arg" in
490	    -l|--list) _copilot_model_list; return 0 ;;
491	    -c|--current)
492	      if [ "$target" = "local" ]; then
493	        printf '%s  (project: %s)\n' "$(_copilot_model_current)" "$settings"
494	      else
495	        printf '%s  (global: %s)\n' "$(_copilot_model_current)" "$statef"
496	      fi
497	      return 0 ;;
498	    -h|--help)
499	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-model [<model-id>|-l|-c]"
500	      printf '%s\n' "  Writes ./.claude/settings.local.json when copilot-here is on,"
501	      printf '%s\n' "  else the global state file used by claude-copilot / copilot-run."
502	      return 0 ;;
503	  esac
504	
505	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
506	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: jq is required" >&2; return 1
507	  fi
508	
509	  local models want resolved
510	  models="$(_copilot_model_list 2>/dev/null)"
511	
512	  # No arg + fzf available → interactive pick.
513	  if [ -z "$arg" ]; then
514	    if ! command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
515	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: pass a model id (fzf not found). Try: copilot-model -l" >&2
516	      return 1
517	    fi
518	    local cur; cur="$(_copilot_model_current)"
519	    want="$(printf '%s\n' "$models" | command fzf --prompt="model> " --height=40% --reverse \
520	      --header="current: $cur")" || { printf '%s\n' "cancelled"; return 0; }
521	    [ -n "$want" ] || { printf '%s\n' "cancelled"; return 0; }
522	    resolved="$want"
523	  else
524	    # "[1m]" is a Claude Code-only 1M-context hint, not a real proxy id:
525	    # strip it for validation, re-append on the resolved id.
526	    local suffix="" base="$arg"
527	    case "$arg" in
528	      *"[1m]") suffix="[1m]"; base="${arg%\[1m\]}" ;;
529	    esac
530	    # Proxy ids are hyphenated (claude-opus-4-8) but muscle memory says
531	    # opus-4.8 — normalize dots to hyphens and accept both.
532	    local norm; norm="$(printf '%s' "$base" | command tr '.' '-')"
533	    # Resolve: exact, else claude-<arg>, else unique substring.
534	    local cand; resolved=""
535	    for cand in "$base" "claude-$base" "$norm" "claude-$norm"; do
536	      if printf '%s\n' "$models" | command grep -qxF "$cand"; then
537	        resolved="$cand"
538	        break
539	      fi
540	    done
541	    if [ -z "$resolved" ]; then
542	      local hits count
543	      hits="$(printf '%s\n' "$models" | command grep -F "$norm" || true)"
544	      count="$(printf '%s\n' "$hits" | command grep -c . )"
545	      if [ "$count" = "1" ] && [ -n "$hits" ]; then
546	        resolved="$hits"
547	      else
548	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: '$arg' did not match a unique model. Try: copilot-model -l" >&2
549	        return 1
550	      fi
551	    fi
552	    resolved="$resolved$suffix"
553	  fi
554	
555	  local old; old="$(_copilot_model_current)"
556	  if [ "$old" = "$resolved" ]; then
557	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: already using $resolved (no change)"
558	    return 0
559	  fi
560	
561	  if [ "$target" = "local" ]; then
562	    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-model.XXXXXX")" || return 1
563	    if jq --arg m "$resolved" \
564	         '.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL = $m | .env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL = $m' \
565	         "$settings" >"$tmp"; then
566	      command mv -- "$tmp" "$settings"
567	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: $old -> $resolved  (project: $settings)"
568	      printf '%s\n' "  ⟳ restart Claude Code to apply (exit, then: claude -c)"
569	    else
570	      command rm -f -- "$tmp"
571	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: failed to update $settings" >&2
572	      return 1
573	    fi
574	  else
575	    command mkdir -p "$(command dirname "$statef")"
576	    printf '%s\n' "$resolved" >"$statef"
577	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: $old -> $resolved  (global: $statef)"
578	    printf '%s\n' "  applies to the next claude-copilot / copilot-run / copilot-here on"
579	  fi
580	}
581
```

```text
1	# Copilot → Claude Code proxy
2	
3	Back [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) with the
4	**Claude models from a GitHub Copilot subscription**, via a local
5	reverse-engineered proxy — the maintained fork
6	[`caozhiyuan/copilot-api`](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api)
7	(npm `@jeffreycao/copilot-api`). The original
8	[`ericc-ch/copilot-api`](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api) is
9	officially unmaintained ([issue #233](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api/issues/233)
10	points at the fork) but still works via `COPILOT_API_PKG=copilot-api@0.7.0`.
11	Both packages share the same token file
12	(`~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`), so switching needs **no re-auth**.
13	
14	- **Shell helpers**: `~/.config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` (`copilot-proxy`, `claude-copilot`, `copilot-run`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model`)
15	- **Runner**: `bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api` (pinned; matches the `bunx` convention in `07_bunx_cli.sh`)
16	- **Not installed by ansible** — pulled on demand via `bunx`, so it stays off the
17	  provisioning path.
18	
19	!!! warning "This violates GitHub Copilot's Terms of Service"
20	    Using a Copilot subscription to power a non-GitHub agent is not permitted, and
21	    copilot-api is reverse-engineered/unofficial. It can trigger GitHub's
22	    **abuse detection** and lead to **temporary suspension of Copilot access**.
23	    Claude Code is token-hungry (frequent background calls, large context) —
24	    note the fork has **no rate limiter** (see Gotchas); `COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1`
25	    reduces background chatter. Use at your own risk; prefer a personal account
26	    over a corporate seat.
27	
28	## Quick start
29	
30	```sh
31	copilot-proxy auth      # one-time: GitHub device login (stores a ghu_ token)
32	
33	claude-copilot          # one-off session on the proxy (auto-starts it; no file writes)
34	
35	copilot-here on         # OR: pin THIS project — plain `claude` uses the proxy
36	copilot-here off        # unpin — back to the real Anthropic backend
37	```
38	
39	## How it works
40	
41	```
42	Claude Code ──Anthropic /v1/messages──▶ copilot-api (localhost:4141)
43	                                          │ native /v1/messages passthrough
44	                                          │ Authorization: Bearer <copilot token>
45	                                          ▼
46	                                   api.githubcopilot.com  (your Copilot sub)
47	```
48	
49	- Claude Code speaks only the **Anthropic Messages API** (`/v1/messages`).
50	- The fork prefers Copilot's **native Anthropic-style `/v1/messages`
51	  endpoint** when available (Enterprise plans:
52	  `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com/v1/messages`) and only falls back to
53	  translating through the OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions`. Native
54	  passthrough is what fixes **extended-thinking blocks**, **WebSearch**
55	  (routed through a Responses-capable GPT model, default `gpt-5-mini`), and
56	  the **infinite tool-retry loops** the original's Anthropic→OpenAI→Anthropic
57	  translation caused.
58	- The original (`copilot-api@0.7.0`) always translates through
59	  `/chat/completions` — thinking blocks are dropped and WebSearch doesn't work.
60	- Claude Code is pointed at the proxy via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` — injected either
61	  as per-process env (`claude-copilot`) or via the gitignored
62	  `./.claude/settings.local.json` (`copilot-here on`). See "Settings-layer design".
63	
64	## Settings-layer design (which file gets the proxy config, and why)
65	
66	Claude Code merges settings low → high: `~/.claude/settings.json` (user) →
67	`./.claude/settings.json` (project, committed) → `./.claude/settings.local.json`
68	(local, gitignored) → CLI flags. The
69	[docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) (and third-party writeups)
70	claim shell env vars beat every settings-file `env` block, but **empirically
71	(verified 2026-07) current Claude Code lets the `settings.local.json` `env`
72	block beat inherited shell env** — see Gotchas.
73	
74	Two of those layers are already owned by other tooling and must stay clean:
75	
76	| Layer | Owner | Why proxy config must NOT go here |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| `~/.claude/settings.json` | chezmoi (`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`) | always-on for *every* project; fights the chezmoi merge |
79	| `./.claude/settings.json` | `claude-plans-here` (`plansDirectory`) | committed to git — proxy config would leak to the team |
80	
81	So the proxy uses the two layers nobody else owns:
82	
83	| Enable | Mechanism | Scope | Disable |
84	|---|---|---|---|
85	| `claude-copilot` / `copilot-run` | per-process env vars | one session | just run plain `claude` next time |
86	| `copilot-here on` | `./.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored) | this project, sticky | `copilot-here off` |
87	
88	```
89	~/.claude/settings.json          .claude/settings.json         shell env                    .claude/settings.local.json
90	(chezmoi: hooks/plugins)    <    (git: plansDirectory)     <   (claude-copilot)         <   (copilot-here on/off)
91	```
92	
93	(Shell env still beats the user- and project-level settings files, so
94	`claude-copilot` works everywhere `copilot-here` is off — it just cannot
95	*override* an active `copilot-here` pin.)
96	
97	## Shell helpers
98	
99	### `copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|logs [N]|whoami|auth]`
100	
101	Manages the background proxy on `$COPILOT_PROXY_PORT` (default `4141`).
102	
103	| Env var | Default | Meaning |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| `COPILOT_PROXY_PORT` | `4141` | port the proxy listens on |
106	| `COPILOT_API_PKG` | `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14` | `bunx` package spec (pin / upgrade; `copilot-api@0.7.0` = old original) |
107	| `COPILOT_PROXY_RATE` | `15` | `--rate-limit` seconds — **original package only** (the fork has no rate limiter) |
108	| `COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET` | `0` | `1` = inject extra quota-saving Claude Code env (see below); off by default because it slightly degrades the UX |
109	
110	Set these in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` (or the per-shell secrets files). `start` refuses
111	to run until `copilot-proxy auth` has stored a token, and waits up to ~20s for the
112	proxy to answer before returning. `start` detects the package flavor from
113	`COPILOT_API_PKG`: only the exact original `copilot-api` gets
114	`--rate-limit`/`--wait` (the fork's `start` doesn't have those flags).
115	
116	`copilot-proxy whoami` is the real login check: it prints your plan / quota
117	(fails loudly if the token is missing or expired). On the fork it queries the
118	running proxy's `/usage` endpoint (jq-summarized) and falls back to
119	`bunx <pkg> debug` when the proxy is down; on the original it runs
120	`check-usage`. Use it instead of eyeballing the token file — the token is a
121	plaintext credential and should not be opened in an editor.
122	
123	### `claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]` — one-off session
124	
125	Layer 1: run a single Claude Code session on the proxy with **zero file
126	writes**. Auto-starts the proxy if it isn't answering, then launches `claude`
127	with the `ANTHROPIC_*` env injected per-process (shell env beats the user- and
128	project-level settings files — but **not** an active `copilot-here` pin in
129	`settings.local.json`; see Gotchas).
130	
131	- Wraps in `specstory run claude` when specstory is installed (markdown
132	  auto-save — same convention as `scode`/`svibe`); opt out with
133	  `--no-specstory`. Extra args reach the claude CLI via specstory's
134	  `-c "custom command"` passthrough: `claude-copilot -c` → continue session.
135	- Revert = nothing to revert; plain `claude` next time is untouched.
136	
137	### `copilot-run <cmd...>` — generic env injector
138	
139	The building block under `claude-copilot`: auto-starts the proxy and runs *any*
140	command with the proxy env. Useful for other Anthropic-compatible tools or a
141	custom specstory invocation:
142	
143	```sh
144	copilot-run specstory run claude    # exactly what claude-copilot does
145	copilot-run claude --resume         # raw claude, no specstory
146	```
147	
148	### `copilot-here [on|off|status]` — sticky per-project toggle
149	
150	Layer 2: pin **this project** to the proxy via `./.claude/settings.local.json`
151	so plain `claude` (and `scode`/`svibe` panes, which just run
152	`specstory run claude`) uses the proxy until you turn it off. Requires `jq`.
153	
154	- `on` — jq-merges the proxy `env` block into `settings.local.json` (creates it
155	  if missing) and makes sure git ignores the file (via `.git/info/exclude`;
156	  Claude Code only auto-gitignores files *it* creates). The committed
157	  `.claude/settings.json` (`plansDirectory` etc.) is never touched.
158	- `off` — removes exactly the env keys `on` added; other content you put in
159	  `settings.local.json` survives, and the file is deleted if it becomes empty.
160	- `status` — pinned? which base URL / model? warns when the proxy isn't running.
161	
162	### `copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c]`
163	
164	Switches the pinned Copilot model. Requires `jq`. Write target — never the
165	committed `.claude/settings.json`:
166	
167	- `copilot-here` is ON in the current project → edits
168	  `./.claude/settings.local.json`.
169	- otherwise → writes the global state file
170	  `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/model`, which `claude-copilot`, `copilot-run`
171	  and the next `copilot-here on` pick up. (`$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL` overrides
172	  the state file; final fallback is `claude-opus-4-8[1m]`.)
173	
174	Behavior:
175	
176	- Fuzzy id: `copilot-model opus-4-8` resolves to `claude-opus-4-8`; dotted
177	  input is normalized (`opus-4.8` works too).
178	- A `[1m]` suffix (`copilot-model 'opus-4-8[1m]'`) is stripped for validation
179	  and re-appended — it's a Claude Code-only 1M-context hint, see the model-id
180	  section below.
181	- Validated against the live proxy `/v1/models` (falls back to a static Claude
182	  list if the proxy is down); typos and ambiguous prefixes are rejected.
183	- No argument → `fzf` picker. `-c` prints the current model and which layer it
184	  came from.
185	- Writes both `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` and `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` —
186	  **the change only takes effect on the next `claude` launch** (env is read at
187	  startup). Switching model does **not** require restarting the proxy.
188	
189	## Injected env (what both layers set)
190	
191	```json
192	{
193	  "env": {
194	    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:4141",
195	    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "dummy",
196	    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "claude-opus-4-8[1m]",
197	    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "claude-opus-4-8[1m]",
198	    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "claude-sonnet-5[1m]",
199	    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "claude-haiku-4-5",
200	    "ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL": "claude-haiku-4-5",
201	    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": "1"
202	  }
203	}
204	```
205	
206	`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is ignored by the proxy but must be set.
207	`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` cuts background chatter (helps with
208	rate limits). Do **not** paste this into the committed `.claude/settings.json` —
209	use `copilot-here on` instead.
210	
211	With `COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1` (opt-in, default off), both layers additionally
212	inject the fork-README quota savers:
213	
214	| Extra env | Effect | UX cost |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0` | no billing/version info in system prompts → avoids prompt-cache invalidation | none noticeable |
217	| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false` | no prompt-suggestion calls | no suggestions |
218	| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY=0` | no away-summary calls | no away summaries |
219	| `DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS=1` | fewer background model calls | fewer niceties (haiku flavor text etc.) |
220	
221	`copilot-here off` removes these keys regardless of the current
222	`COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET` value.
223	
224	## Gotchas (these cost real debugging time)
225	
226	### `settings.local.json` env beats shell env (docs say otherwise)
227	
228	Verified empirically (2026-07): current Claude Code lets the `env` block of
229	`./.claude/settings.local.json` **override inherited shell env vars** — the
230	opposite of what the official settings docs imply. Consequences:
231	
232	- `claude-copilot` / `copilot-run` **cannot** redirect a project where
233	  `copilot-here on` is active (harmless when both point at the same proxy,
234	  silently wrong when they don't).
235	- Trialing another proxy/port via the wrapper requires `copilot-here off`
236	  first.
237	
238	### The fork has no rate limiter
239	
240	The fork's `start` dropped `--rate-limit`/`--wait`. Its README's mitigation is
241	reducing Claude Code's chatter instead — that's exactly what
242	`COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1` injects (off by default here; we prioritize UX over
243	Copilot quota). If you really want request throttling, fall back to the
244	original: `COPILOT_API_PKG=copilot-api@0.7.0`.
245	
246	### Fork wart: `context_management` can 400
247	
248	Newer Claude Code context-editing may inject `context_management`, which
249	Copilot's native `/v1/messages` endpoint rejects with a 400
250	([caozhiyuan#305](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api/issues/305),
251	version-dependent). Real Claude Code runs didn't trigger it in testing, but if
252	you see unexplained 400s on long sessions, check that issue first.
253	
254	### Do not use Claude Code's `/model` picker
255	
256	It sends Anthropic's *official* dated ids (e.g. `claude-opus-4-8-YYYYMMDD`),
257	which the Copilot backend rejects:
258	
259	```
260	API Error: 400 {"error":{"message":"The requested model is not supported.",
261	"code":"model_not_supported", ...}}
262	```
263	
264	Pin the model with `copilot-model` instead — undated hyphenated ids
265	(`claude-opus-4-8`) work; only the picker's dated ids fail.
266	
267	### Dotted ids cause the "[Opus 4] retired" warning and a >100% context HUD
268	
269	Historic gotcha, fixed by the hyphenated defaults. With a **dotted** id
270	(`claude-opus-4.8`, the only shape the original proxy accepted), Claude Code
271	fails to match its built-in model table, so it:
272	
273	- displays `[Opus 4]` and warns *"Claude Opus 4 was retired"* (falls back to
274	  the nearest known, retired name), and
275	- assumes a **200k** context window, while Copilot actually serves opus-4-8 /
276	  sonnet-5 with **1M** (`max_context_window_tokens: 1000000` in `/v1/models`)
277	  — so HUD/statusline context can read >100% and compaction triggers on the
278	  wrong budget.
279	
280	The fix is the id shape the helpers now inject by default:
281	**`claude-opus-4-8[1m]`** — hyphenated so Claude Code recognizes the family
282	(correct display name, no retirement warning), plus the `[1m]` suffix so it
283	sizes context to 1M. Claude Code strips `[1m]` before sending, so the proxy
284	sees a valid id (a *literal* `...[1m]` in a raw API call is rejected —
285	`copilot-model` handles the stripping when validating).
286	
287	### The token gotcha: `gho_` vs `ghu_`
288	
289	There are two different GitHub tokens, and they are **not** interchangeable:
290	
291	| Source | Prefix | `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange |
292	|---|---|---|
293	| OpenCode's stored auth | `gho_` | **fails (404)** |
294	| `copilot-proxy auth` (device login) | `ghu_` | **works** |
295	
296	OpenCode's `gho_` token (OAuth App) works only when used *directly* as a Bearer
297	against `api.githubcopilot.com`; it cannot complete copilot-api's classic
298	token-exchange step. **Let `copilot-proxy auth` mint its own `ghu_` token — do not
299	reuse OpenCode's.** Token is stored at `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`.
300	
301	## Available Claude model ids
302	
303	Verified via `/v1/models` + `/v1/messages` (2026-07): `claude-opus-4-5`,
304	`claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`,
305	`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`. The fork accepts
306	both hyphenated and legacy dotted (`claude-opus-4.8`) forms at request time,
307	but **use hyphenated ids in Claude Code** — dotted ids break its model
308	detection (see Gotchas). Context windows from `/v1/models` capabilities:
309	opus-4-8 and sonnet-5 are **1M** (`max_prompt_tokens: 936000`), haiku-4-5 is
310	200k — append `[1m]` to the 1M models so Claude Code knows. Non-Claude models
311	(gpt-5.5, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, …) are also served — see `copilot-model -l`
312	or `GET /v1/models`.
313	
314	## Useful commands
315	
316	```sh
317	claude-copilot                       # one-off proxy session (specstory-wrapped)
318	copilot-here status                  # is this project pinned to the proxy?
319	copilot-model -c                     # current model + which layer it came from
320	copilot-proxy status                 # up? which Claude models?
321	copilot-proxy whoami                 # validate token → account / plan / quota
322	copilot-proxy logs 60                # tail the proxy log
323	# usage dashboard (bundled locally by the fork):
324	#   http://localhost:4141/usage-viewer?endpoint=http://localhost:4141/usage
325	```
326

338	  this design deliberately stays out of
339	- OpenCode's native GitHub Copilot provider (no proxy needed for OpenCode itself)

561	### Proxy helpers
562	
563	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.
564	
565	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
566	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
567	| `withproxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a single command with proxy env vars exported to the child only (e.g. `withproxy curl ...`) |
568	| `try_direct_then_proxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a command direct; on failure, retry via `withproxy`. Used as the default for reader functions. |
569	| `proxy-on` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Export `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` in the current shell |
570	| `proxy-off` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Unset all proxy env vars in the current shell |
571	| `proxy-status` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Report state: **active** (exported), **available** (detected), or **unavailable** |
572	| `proxy-test` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Test detected proxy egress with `curl https://www.google.com/generate_204` (HTTP, not ICMP ping) |
573	| `proxy-refresh` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Clear cached detection, re-probe, print status (use after toggling your proxy) |
574

577	> Render web pages as markdown in the terminal. All functions use `try_direct_then_proxy` so non-GFW'd URLs pay zero proxy overhead. Pick the extractor by function name. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md).

582	| `readlocal` | function | `dot_config/shell/55_web_reader.sh` | Read article via trafilatura + glow (local, offline) *(requires `trafilatura`)* |
583	| `readnode` | function | `dot_config/shell/55_web_reader.sh` | Read article via readability-cli (`readable`) + glow (Mozilla Readability) *(requires `readable`)* |

660	## macOS apps
661	
662	> Graceful GUI app control via `osascript` + Apple Events. Prefer over `killall` for apps with state (OrbStack, Docker Desktop, Slack, etc.) — `quit` sends ⌘Q-equivalent, letting the app tear down cleanly. App NAME is the AppleScript name (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not bundle ID; passed via `osascript argv` so spaces/quotes are safe.
663	
664	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
665	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
666	| `appquit <AppName>` | function | `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` (macOS), `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (Linux) | **Cross-platform.** macOS: Quit Apple Event (graceful, equivalent to ⌘Q). Linux: `pkill -TERM -f <pattern>` resolved from `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` overrides or auto-derived from `.desktop` scan; Electron + Firefox honour SIGTERM as graceful quit. |
667	| `applaunch <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch in background (no focus steal). Linux: `gtk-launch <desktop-id>` via `setsid -f`. App-defined startup behaviour applies. |
668	| `appactivate <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch + bring to front. Linux: D-Bus call to GNOME `window-calls` extension if installed (best fidelity), otherwise falls back to `applaunch` (single-instance apps re-focus). |
669	| `apprestart <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** `appquit` + poll until process gone (≤15s) + `applaunch`. On Linux, launches the app even if it wasn't running (mirrors macOS silent-quit semantics). |
670	| `apprunning <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Silent predicate; exit 0 if running, 1 otherwise. Linux backend: `pgrep -f <pattern>`. |
671	| `applist [--pids\|--all]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Default: names of running apps the helper recognises. `--pids` adds `<pid>\t<name>` (used by `tv {mac,linux}-apps`). macOS lists foreground GUI apps via System Events; Linux enumerates registered overrides + auto-derived from `.desktop` scan filtered to running processes. Linux `--all` shows non-running entries too. |
672	| `appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, divergent fidelity.** macOS: best-effort "Not Responding" via timed-out Apple Event. Linux: only meaningful for apps registered with `--mpris=NAME` (Spotify, mpv, VLC); for Electron/Firefox/most apps it degrades to `apprunning` with a stderr note — no public Linux API analog to macOS Apple Events. |
673	| `linux_app_register NAME [OPTS]` | function | `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` | **Linux-only.** Register an app for the Linux `app-*` helpers — `--desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]`. Typical call site: `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (sourced at shell startup, never auto-stubbed). Override file matters for AppImage / Snap / Flatpak where auto-derivation can't resolve the runtime binary path — see `pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md`. `linux_app_register --list` prints the current registry. |

692	## System audio & playback
693	
694	> Control **system volume / mute / playback / now-playing** from the shell. Cross-platform `sys*` verbs with the same names on both OSes (macOS `osascript`; Linux `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` + `playerctl`). Two tiers: `sysvol`/`sysmute` are **built-in** (always work, no extra tools); `sysplay`/`sysnow` need the **extended** tools from `installMediaControl=true`, degrading gracefully with an install hint otherwise. Remote one-key mute: `fleet exec --login --group all -- sysmute on`. Full story + caveats: [docs/tools/media-control.md](../tools/media-control.md).
695	
696	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
697	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
698	| `sysvol [N\|+N\|-N]` | function | `dot_config/shell/57_macos_audio.sh.tmpl` (macOS), `dot_config/shell/57_linux_audio.sh.tmpl` (Linux) | **Cross-platform, built-in.** No arg prints current output volume (0–100); `N` sets absolute; `+N`/`-N` adjusts relative. macOS via `osascript`; Linux via first of `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` (override `SYSAUDIO_BACKEND`). |
699	| `sysmute [on\|off\|toggle]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, built-in.** Mute system output; default `toggle`. The remote one-key-mute primitive. |
700	| `sysplay [next\|previous]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, extended.** No arg toggles play/pause; `next`/`previous` skip. macOS: `nowplaying-cli` (any app) or per-app AppleScript fallback (Music/Spotify). Linux: `playerctl` (MPRIS). Prints install hint if the extended tool is absent. |
701	| `sysnow` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, extended.** Print the currently playing track (`Artist - Title`). ⚠ macOS 15.4+ locked the MediaRemote API, so this covers Music/Spotify only (not web audio); Linux reads any MPRIS player via `playerctl`. |

729	## Tmux Integration
730	
731	> Requires tmux + OSC 133 markers in the pane's scrollback (emitted by [`02_shell_integration.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh) — if missing, run `exec zsh` to reload). All three functions print to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`) AND copy to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge. Shell-level counterparts of the `prefix + M-y` / `M-i` tmux bindings — see [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 133](../tools/tmux/README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style).

734	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
735	| `cpout [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's output** (default N=1). Accepts positional integer for lookback |
736	| `cpcmd [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's input line** (default N=1). Reads zsh history so works outside tmux too |
737	| `cpblock [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's full block** (prompt + input + output). Default N=1 |
738	| `tsum [-d\|--shallow] [-r] [-i] [--sort closability] [--only TIER] [--dry-run]` | function | `dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh` | AI-summarize every tmux session — one-glance "what is this session", with closability tiers (🟢 safe / 🟡 check / 🔴 keep). Reuses the AI Capture agent fallback (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent); 10-min cached in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/`. `-d` includes the visible area of each session's active pane (20-100 lines, self-capture skipped); set `TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1` in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` to make `-d` implicit (override with `--shallow`). `--sort closability` orders keep → check → safe (default: alphabetical); `--only {safe,check,keep}` filters to one tier. `-r` bypasses cache; `-i` opens fzf picker that switches client on Enter (also reachable via tmux `prefix + Space → Sessions → AI session summary`); `--dry-run` prints the prompt without calling the LLM. **On hosts with multiple tmux binaries** (apt + appimage, brew + system) export `TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/path/to/tmux` so tsum talks to the right server. |

742	## AI Capture
743	
744	> One-shot pipeline: capture a past block (via `cpblock N`) and pass it to a coding-agent CLI (opencode / claude / codex / agyc / cursor-agent) in non-interactive / advisory mode. Agent auto-detected in `$AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY` order; override with `-a AGENT`. Prompt override via `-p PROMPT`. Agent reply goes to stdout (pipe-friendly: `aifix | tee /tmp/advice.md`), status line to stderr.
745	
746	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
747	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
748	| `aifix [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Capture Nth block (tmux), ask agent to diagnose + suggest a fix |
749	| `aiexplain [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Capture Nth block (tmux), ask agent to explain what happened |
750	| `aifix-stdin [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Non-tmux: read stdin as context, ask agent (`tail -100 log \| aifix-stdin`) |
751	| `aifix-run -- CMD [ARG...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Non-tmux: run CMD with stdout+stderr teed, feed to agent |
752	| `aifix-rerun [-y]` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Non-tmux: thefuck-style re-execute last command (confirms unless `-y`; side-effect warning) |
753	| `aiblock` | function | `dot_config/shell/04_ai_capture.sh` | Launch the `scripts/aiblock.py` TUI: pick command(s) from history, edit prompt, pick action (print / copy / spawn new agent window). Deps resolved via `uv run --script` |

757	## AI Run
758	
759	> Quick "run one prompt through a coding agent" wrappers — fresh prompt, streams the reply straight back.
