```text
1	# 43_copilot_proxy.sh - GitHub Copilot -> Anthropic/OpenAI proxy for Claude Code
2	#   (shared bash + zsh).
3	#
4	# Runs the maintained copilot-api fork (caozhiyuan/copilot-api, npm
5	# @jeffreycao/copilot-api) so a GitHub Copilot subscription can back Claude Code
6	# (and any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible client). The original ericc-ch/copilot-api
7	# is unmaintained (its issue #233 points at the fork) but still works via
8	# COPILOT_API_PKG=copilot-api@0.7.0 — flags differ per package, see
9	# _copilot_pkg_flavor. Both packages share the same token file, so switching
10	# needs no re-auth. Full guide + risks: docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md.
11	#
12	# Public surface:
13	#   copilot-proxy [start|stop|status|restart|logs|whoami|auth]   - manage the proxy
14	#   copilot-run <cmd...>       - run any command with the proxy env injected
15	#                                (auto-starts the proxy first)
16	#   claude-copilot [args...]   - one-off Claude Code session on the proxy
17	#                                (specstory-wrapped when available; zero file writes)
18	#   copilot-here [on|off|status] - sticky per-project toggle via the gitignored
19	#                                ./.claude/settings.local.json (never touches the
20	#                                committed .claude/settings.json)
21	#   copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c] - switch the pinned model (edits settings.local.json
22	#                                when copilot-here is on, else the global state file)
23	#
24	# Settings-layer design (why settings.local.json / env vars, and NOT the
25	# committed .claude/settings.json nor ~/.claude/settings.json):
26	#   - ~/.claude/settings.json is chezmoi-managed (dot_claude/modify_settings.json)
27	#     and would make the proxy always-on for every project.
28	#   - ./.claude/settings.json is committed (claude-plans-here puts plansDirectory
29	#     there) — proxy config must not leak into git.
30	#   - Claude Code precedence (low→high): user < project < settings.local.json
31	#     (gitignored) < CLI flags. GOTCHA (verified 2026-07): current Claude Code
32	#     lets the settings.local.json env block BEAT inherited shell env vars —
33	#     so copilot-run/claude-copilot cannot override a project where
34	#     `copilot-here on` points elsewhere (run `copilot-here off` first).
35	#
36	# Portability notes (POSIX subset, both shells source this file):
37	#   - runs the proxy via `bunx` (matches 07_bunx_cli.sh); pinned version avoids a
38	#     per-launch @latest registry round-trip. Override with COPILOT_API_PKG.
39	#   - no ZLE/compdef/setopt/glob-qualifiers here (bash would error on source).
40	#
41	# Env (set in ~/.shellrc.adhoc or ~/.config/{zsh/secrets.zsh,bash/secrets.sh}):
42	#   COPILOT_PROXY_PORT   default: 4141        - port the proxy listens on
43	#   COPILOT_API_PKG      default: @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14
44	#                                             - bunx package spec (pin/upgrade;
45	#                                               copilot-api@0.7.0 = old original)
46	#   COPILOT_PROXY_RATE   default: 15          - --rate-limit seconds; ONLY used
47	#                                               by the original package (the fork
48	#                                               has no rate limiter)
49	#   COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET  default: 0           - 1 = inject extra quota-saving env
50	#                                               (fewer background calls, but a
51	#                                               slightly degraded Claude Code UX)
52	
53	# --- shared constants / helpers -------------------------------------------------
54	
55	_copilot_port() { printf '%s' "${COPILOT_PROXY_PORT:-4141}"; }
56	_copilot_pkg()  { printf '%s' "${COPILOT_API_PKG:-@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14}"; }
57	
58	# CLI flavor from the package spec: the ORIGINAL bare `copilot-api` takes
59	# --rate-limit/--wait and has `check-usage`; the fork (and anything else)
60	# doesn't. Strips a trailing @version, but not the @scope/ prefix.
61	_copilot_pkg_flavor() {
62	  local name; name="$(_copilot_pkg)"
63	  case "$name" in
64	    copilot-api|copilot-api@*) printf 'original' ;;
65	    *) printf 'fork' ;;
66	  esac
67	}
68	_copilot_base() { printf 'http://localhost:%s' "$(_copilot_port)"; }
69	_copilot_logfile() { printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-api-$(_copilot_port).log"; }
70	_copilot_pidfile() { printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-api-$(_copilot_port).pid"; }
71	
72	# Global default-model state file (used by copilot-run/claude-copilot when the
73	# project has no copilot-here pin). Written by `copilot-model`.
74	_copilot_model_state() {
75	  printf '%s' "${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/copilot-proxy/model"
76	}
77	
78	# Resolve the model for env injection: $COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL > state file > default.
79	#
80	# Model-id shape matters (verified 2026-07):
81	#   - HYPHENATED ids (claude-opus-4-8), not dotted (claude-opus-4.8): Claude
82	#     Code only recognizes hyphenated family names — dotted ids fall back to
83	#     a legacy "[Opus 4] retired" label AND a 200k context assumption.
84	#   - "[1m]" suffix: Copilot serves opus-4-8 / sonnet-5 with a 1M context
85	#     window; the suffix makes Claude Code strip it, send the context-1m
86	#     beta header, and size HUD/compaction to 1M (otherwise it assumes 200k
87	#     and shows >100% context). Claude Code-only: raw API clients must send
88	#     the plain id — the proxy rejects a literal "...[1m]" model.
89	_copilot_default_model() {
90	  if [ -n "${COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL:-}" ]; then
91	    printf '%s' "$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL"
92	  elif [ -f "$(_copilot_model_state)" ]; then
93	    command head -n 1 "$(_copilot_model_state)"
94	  else
95	    printf '%s' "claude-opus-4-8[1m]"
96	  fi
97	}
98	
99	# Is the proxy answering on its port?
100	_copilot_alive() {
101	  command curl -fsS --max-time 2 "$(_copilot_base)/v1/models" >/dev/null 2>&1
102	}
103	
104	# --- proxy manager --------------------------------------------------------------
105	
106	# Manage the copilot-api proxy. Subcommands: start|stop|status|restart|logs|auth.
107	# Example:
108	#   copilot-proxy start          # background-start on $COPILOT_PROXY_PORT
109	#   copilot-proxy status         # is it up? which models?
110	copilot-proxy() {
111	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
112	    emulate -L zsh
113	    setopt localoptions pipefail
114	  else
115	    set -o pipefail
116	  fi
117	
118	  if ! command -v bunx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
119	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: bunx not found (needs bun via mise)." >&2
120	    return 1
121	  fi
122	
123	  local port pkg logf pidf
124	  port="$(_copilot_port)"; pkg="$(_copilot_pkg)"
125	  logf="$(_copilot_logfile)"; pidf="$(_copilot_pidfile)"
126	
127	  local action="${1:-status}"
128	  case "$action" in
129	    start)
130	      if _copilot_alive; then
131	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: already running on port $port" >&2
132	        return 0
133	      fi
134	      # First run needs `copilot-proxy auth` to store a ghu_ token; warn if absent.
135	      if [ ! -f "$HOME/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token" ]; then
136	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not authenticated yet — run 'copilot-proxy auth' first." >&2
137	        return 1
138	      fi
139	      # Flag sets differ per package: only the original has --rate-limit/--wait
140	      # (the fork ships no rate limiter — mitigate with COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1).
141	      if [ "$(_copilot_pkg_flavor)" = "original" ]; then
142	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: starting ($pkg) on port $port (rate-limit ${COPILOT_PROXY_RATE:-15}s) ..."
143	        # nohup + background; detach so it survives the shell. Log to a file.
144	        nohup bunx "$pkg" start \
145	          --port "$port" \
146	          --rate-limit "${COPILOT_PROXY_RATE:-15}" \
147	          --wait \
148	          >"$logf" 2>&1 &
149	      else
150	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: starting ($pkg) on port $port ..."
151	        nohup bunx "$pkg" start \
152	          --port "$port" \
153	          >"$logf" 2>&1 &
154	      fi
155	      printf '%s\n' "$!" >"$pidf"
156	      # Wait up to ~20s for it to answer.
157	      local i=0
158	      while [ "$i" -lt 20 ]; do
159	        if _copilot_alive; then
160	          printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: up → $(_copilot_base)  (logs: copilot-proxy logs)"
161	          return 0
162	        fi
163	        sleep 1
164	        i=$((i + 1))
165	      done
166	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: did not come up in time — check 'copilot-proxy logs'." >&2
167	      return 1
168	      ;;
169	    stop)
170	      # Prefer the tracked pid; fall back to a broad match.
171	      if [ -f "$pidf" ]; then
172	        local pid; pid="$(cat "$pidf" 2>/dev/null)"
173	        [ -n "$pid" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null
174	        command rm -f -- "$pidf"
175	      fi
176	      command pkill -f "copilot-api.*--port $port" 2>/dev/null
177	      sleep 1
178	      if _copilot_alive; then
179	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: still answering on $port (another instance?)" >&2
180	        return 1
181	      fi
182	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: stopped (port $port free)"
183	      ;;
184	    restart)
185	      copilot-proxy stop
186	      copilot-proxy start
187	      ;;
188	    status)
189	      if _copilot_alive; then
190	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: RUNNING on $(_copilot_base)"
191	        printf '%s\n' "  models: $(command curl -fsS --max-time 3 "$(_copilot_base)/v1/models" 2>/dev/null \
192	          | command grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | command sed 's/"id":"//;s/"//' | command grep -i claude | command tr '\n' ' ')"
193	      else
194	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not running on port $port  (start: copilot-proxy start)"
195	        return 1
196	      fi
197	      ;;
198	    logs)
199	      if [ -f "$logf" ]; then command tail -n "${2:-40}" "$logf"; else
200	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: no log file at $logf" >&2; return 1; fi
201	      ;;
202	    auth)
203	      # One-time device login → stores a ghu_ token copilot-api can exchange.
204	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: launching copilot-api device login ..."
205	      bunx "$pkg" auth
206	      ;;
207	    whoami|usage)
208	      # Real login check: exchanges the stored token against GitHub and prints
209	      # the account / plan / quota. Fails loudly if the token is missing/expired.
210	      if [ ! -f "$HOME/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token" ]; then
211	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not authenticated — run 'copilot-proxy auth' first." >&2
212	        return 1
213	      fi
214	      if [ "$(_copilot_pkg_flavor)" = "original" ]; then
215	        bunx "$pkg" check-usage
216	      elif _copilot_alive; then
217	        # Fork has no check-usage subcommand; its /usage endpoint serves the
218	        # GitHub quota payload (same data as the bundled /usage-viewer).
219	        if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
220	          command curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$(_copilot_base)/usage" | jq '{
221	            plan: (.copilot_plan // .access_type_sku // "unknown"),
222	            quota_reset: (.quota_reset_date // null),
223	            quotas: ((.quota_snapshots // {}) | map_values(
224	              if type == "object" then
225	                {remaining, entitlement, percent_remaining, unlimited}
226	              else . end))
227	          }'
228	        else
229	          command curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$(_copilot_base)/usage"
230	        fi
231	      else
232	        # Proxy down → the fork's `debug` still validates auth state / paths.
233	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: not running — showing auth/debug info instead of quota." >&2
234	        bunx "$pkg" debug
235	      fi
236	      ;;
237	    -h|--help|help)
238	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|logs [N]|whoami|auth]"
239	      ;;
240	    *)
241	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: unknown action '$action' (try --help)" >&2
242	      return 1
243	      ;;
244	  esac
245	}
246	
247	# --- session wrapper (Layer 1: one-off, zero file writes) ------------------------
248	
249	# Run any command with the copilot-proxy env injected (per-process only —
250	# nothing is written to disk). Auto-starts the proxy when it isn't answering.
251	# GOTCHA (verified 2026-07): current Claude Code lets the settings.local.json
252	# env block beat inherited shell env, so this does NOT win inside a project
253	# where `copilot-here on` pins something else — `copilot-here off` first.
254	# Example:
255	#   copilot-run claude                      # raw Claude Code on the proxy
256	#   copilot-run specstory run claude        # specstory-wrapped session
257	copilot-run() {
258	  if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
259	    printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-run <cmd> [args...]   (injects ANTHROPIC_* proxy env)" >&2
260	    return 1
261	  fi
262	  if ! _copilot_alive; then
263	    copilot-proxy start || return 1
264	  fi
265	  local model; model="$(_copilot_default_model)"
266	  # Opt-in quota savers (COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1): prepended as NAME=VALUE args
267	  # to `env`. Off by default — they degrade the Claude Code UX a little.
268	  if [ "${COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET:-0}" = "1" ]; then
269	    set -- \
270	      CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER="0" \
271	      CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION="false" \
272	      CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY="0" \
273	      DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS="1" \
274	      "$@"
275	  fi
276	  # `command env` (not bare var-prefix) so the vars are strictly per-process:
277	  # POSIX var-prefix on a *function* call would leak into the current shell.
278	  command env \
279	    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="$(_copilot_base)" \
280	    ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="dummy" \
281	    ANTHROPIC_MODEL="$model" \
282	    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="$model" \
283	    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="claude-sonnet-5[1m]" \
284	    ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="claude-haiku-4-5" \
285	    ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL="claude-haiku-4-5" \
286	    CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC="1" \
287	    "$@"
288	}
289	
290	# One-off Claude Code session backed by the Copilot proxy. Nothing on disk
291	# changes — revert is just running plain `claude` next time.
292	# Wraps in `specstory run` when specstory is installed (markdown auto-save,
293	# same convention as scode/svibe); opt out with --no-specstory. Extra args go
294	# to the claude CLI (via specstory's -c "custom command" passthrough).
295	# Example:
296	#   claude-copilot                 # specstory run claude (proxy env)
297	#   claude-copilot -c              # continue last session
298	#   claude-copilot --no-specstory  # raw claude, no markdown auto-save
299	claude-copilot() {
300	  local ss="auto"
301	  case "${1:-}" in
302	    --no-specstory) ss="never"; shift ;;
303	    --specstory)    shift ;;
304	    -h|--help)
305	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
306	      printf '%s\n' "  One-off Claude Code session on the Copilot proxy (no file writes)."
307	      printf '%s\n' "  Sticky per-project instead: copilot-here on"
308	      return 0 ;;
309	  esac
310	  if [ "$ss" = "auto" ] && command -v specstory >/dev/null 2>&1; then
311	    if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
312	      copilot-run specstory run claude -c "claude $*"
313	    else
314	      copilot-run specstory run claude
315	    fi
316	  else
317	    copilot-run claude "$@"
318	  fi
319	}
320	
321	# --- per-project toggle (Layer 2: sticky, gitignored settings.local.json) --------
322	
323	# Env keys we own in .claude/settings.local.json (kept in one place so `off`
324	# removes exactly what `on` added — including the COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET extras,
325	# regardless of the knob's value at `off` time).
326	_copilot_here_keys='["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL","ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN","ANTHROPIC_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL","ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL","CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC","CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER","CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION","CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY","DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS"]'
327	
328	# Pin THIS project to the Copilot proxy via ./.claude/settings.local.json —
329	# the gitignored local layer that overrides the committed .claude/settings.json
330	# (so claude-plans-here's plansDirectory stays untouched). Plain `claude` then
331	# uses the proxy here until `copilot-here off`.
332	# Example:
333	#   copilot-here on        # pin project to the proxy
334	#   copilot-here status    # pinned? which model?
335	#   copilot-here off       # unpin (removes only our env keys)
336	copilot-here() {
337	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
338	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: jq is required" >&2; return 1
339	  fi
340	
341	  local settings=".claude/settings.local.json"
342	  local action="${1:-status}"
343	  case "$action" in
344	    on)
345	      command mkdir -p .claude
346	      local base='{}'
347	      [ -f "$settings" ] && base="$(command cat "$settings")"
348	      [ -n "$base" ] || base='{}'
349	      local model; model="$(_copilot_default_model)"
350	      local quiet="${COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET:-0}"
351	      local tmp; tmp="$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-here.XXXXXX")" || return 1
352	      if printf '%s' "$base" | jq \
353	          --arg base_url "$(_copilot_base)" --arg model "$model" --arg quiet "$quiet" '
354	          .env = ((.env // {}) + {
355	            ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: $base_url,
356	            ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: "dummy",
357	            ANTHROPIC_MODEL: $model,
358	            ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: $model,
359	            ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: "claude-sonnet-5[1m]",
360	            ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: "claude-haiku-4-5",
361	            ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL: "claude-haiku-4-5",
362	            CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: "1"
363	          } + (if $quiet == "1" then {
364	            CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER: "0",
365	            CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION: "false",
366	            CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY: "0",
367	            DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS: "1"
368	          } else {} end))' >"$tmp"; then
369	        command mv -- "$tmp" "$settings"
370	      else
371	        command rm -f -- "$tmp"
372	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: jq failed; $settings unchanged" >&2
373	        return 1
374	      fi
375	      # Claude Code only auto-gitignores settings.local.json when IT creates the
376	      # file — since we created it, belt-and-braces via .git/info/exclude.
377	      if command git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
378	        if ! command git check-ignore -q "$settings" 2>/dev/null; then
379	          local exclude; exclude="$(command git rev-parse --git-dir)/info/exclude"
380	          printf '%s\n' ".claude/settings.local.json" >>"$exclude"
381	        fi
382	      fi
383	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: ON — $settings pins Claude Code to $(_copilot_base) (model: $model)"
384	      printf '%s\n' "  plain \`claude\` in this project now uses the proxy (restart any running session)"
385	      _copilot_alive || printf '%s\n' "  ⚠ proxy not running — start it with: copilot-proxy start"
386	      ;;
387	    off)
388	      if [ ! -f "$settings" ]; then
389	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: already off (no $settings)"
390	        return 0
391	      fi
392	      local tmp; tmp="$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-here.XXXXXX")" || return 1
393	      # Remove only OUR env keys; drop .env when it empties; keep other content.
394	      if jq --argjson keys "$_copilot_here_keys" '
395	          .env = ((.env // {}) | with_entries(select(.key as $k | ($keys | index($k)) == null)))
396	          | if .env == {} then del(.env) else . end' \
397	          "$settings" >"$tmp"; then
398	        if [ "$(jq -r 'if . == {} then "empty" else "kept" end' "$tmp")" = "empty" ]; then
399	          command rm -f -- "$tmp" "$settings"
400	          printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: OFF — removed $settings (it held only proxy config)"
401	        else
402	          command mv -- "$tmp" "$settings"
403	          printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: OFF — proxy env removed from $settings (other content kept)"
404	        fi
405	        printf '%s\n' "  plain \`claude\` is back on the real Anthropic backend (restart any running session)"
406	      else
407	        command rm -f -- "$tmp"
408	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: jq failed; $settings unchanged" >&2
409	        return 1
410	      fi
411	      ;;
412	    status)
413	      if [ -f "$settings" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL // empty' "$settings" 2>/dev/null)" != "" ]; then
414	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: ON  (base: $(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL' "$settings"), model: $(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL // "(unset)"' "$settings"))"
415	        _copilot_alive || printf '%s\n' "  ⚠ proxy not running — start it with: copilot-proxy start"
416	      else
417	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: off  (enable: copilot-here on; one-off: claude-copilot)"
418	        return 1
419	      fi
420	      ;;
421	    -h|--help|help)
422	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-here [on|off|status]   (toggles ./.claude/settings.local.json)"
423	      ;;
424	    *)
425	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-here: unknown action '$action' (try --help)" >&2
426	      return 1
427	      ;;
428	  esac
429	}
430	
431	# --- model switcher -------------------------------------------------------------
432	
433	# Switch which Copilot model is pinned. Claude Code's own /model picker sends
434	# dated Anthropic ids the Copilot backend rejects (model_not_supported), so pin
435	# here. Use the HYPHENATED ids the proxy lists (claude-opus-4-8); an optional
436	# "[1m]" suffix tells Claude Code the model has a 1M context window (see
437	# _copilot_default_model) — it is stripped before validating against the proxy.
438	#
439	# Write target (never the committed .claude/settings.json):
440	#   - copilot-here is ON in this project → ./.claude/settings.local.json
441	#   - otherwise → global state file (~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/model), which
442	#     claude-copilot / copilot-run / the next `copilot-here on` pick up.
443	# Example:
444	#   copilot-model opus-4-8         # fuzzy → claude-opus-4-8 (opus-4.8 works too)
445	#   copilot-model 'opus-4-8[1m]'   # same + 1M-context hint for Claude Code
446	#   copilot-model -l               # list available (live from proxy)
447	#   copilot-model -c               # print current (+ where it came from)
448	copilot-model() {
449	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
450	    emulate -L zsh
451	    setopt localoptions pipefail
452	  else
453	    set -o pipefail
454	  fi
455	
456	  local settings=".claude/settings.local.json"
457	  local statef; statef="$(_copilot_model_state)"
458	
459	  # copilot-here mode? (local settings file carries our proxy env)
460	  local target="state"
461	  if [ -f "$settings" ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 \
462	     && [ "$(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL // empty' "$settings" 2>/dev/null)" != "" ]; then
463	    target="local"
464	  fi
465	
466	  # List available model ids (live proxy, else a static Claude fallback).
467	  _copilot_model_list() {
468	    local json
469	    if json="$(command curl -fsS --max-time 3 "$(_copilot_base)/v1/models" 2>/dev/null)"; then
470	      printf '%s\n' "$json" | command grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | command sed 's/"id":"//;s/"//' | command sort
471	    else
472	      printf '%s\n' \
473	        claude-opus-4-8 claude-opus-4-7 claude-opus-4-6 claude-opus-4-5 \
474	        claude-sonnet-5 claude-sonnet-4-6 claude-sonnet-4-5 claude-haiku-4-5
475	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: proxy not reachable — showing fallback list" >&2
476	    fi
477	  }
478	
479	  # Current pinned model, from whichever layer is active.
480	  _copilot_model_current() {
481	    if [ "$target" = "local" ]; then
482	      jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL // "(unset)"' "$settings"
483	    else
484	      _copilot_default_model
485	    fi
486	  }
487	
488	  local arg="${1:-}"
489	  case "$arg" in
490	    -l|--list) _copilot_model_list; return 0 ;;
491	    -c|--current)
492	      if [ "$target" = "local" ]; then
493	        printf '%s  (project: %s)\n' "$(_copilot_model_current)" "$settings"
494	      else
495	        printf '%s  (global: %s)\n' "$(_copilot_model_current)" "$statef"
496	      fi
497	      return 0 ;;
498	    -h|--help)
499	      printf '%s\n' "Usage: copilot-model [<model-id>|-l|-c]"
500	      printf '%s\n' "  Writes ./.claude/settings.local.json when copilot-here is on,"
501	      printf '%s\n' "  else the global state file used by claude-copilot / copilot-run."
502	      return 0 ;;
503	  esac
504	
505	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
506	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: jq is required" >&2; return 1
507	  fi
508	
509	  local models want resolved
510	  models="$(_copilot_model_list 2>/dev/null)"
511	
512	  # No arg + fzf available → interactive pick.
513	  if [ -z "$arg" ]; then
514	    if ! command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
515	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: pass a model id (fzf not found). Try: copilot-model -l" >&2
516	      return 1
517	    fi
518	    local cur; cur="$(_copilot_model_current)"
519	    want="$(printf '%s\n' "$models" | command fzf --prompt="model> " --height=40% --reverse \
520	      --header="current: $cur")" || { printf '%s\n' "cancelled"; return 0; }
521	    [ -n "$want" ] || { printf '%s\n' "cancelled"; return 0; }
522	    resolved="$want"
523	  else
524	    # "[1m]" is a Claude Code-only 1M-context hint, not a real proxy id:
525	    # strip it for validation, re-append on the resolved id.
526	    local suffix="" base="$arg"
527	    case "$arg" in
528	      *"[1m]") suffix="[1m]"; base="${arg%\[1m\]}" ;;
529	    esac
530	    # Proxy ids are hyphenated (claude-opus-4-8) but muscle memory says
531	    # opus-4.8 — normalize dots to hyphens and accept both.
532	    local norm; norm="$(printf '%s' "$base" | command tr '.' '-')"
533	    # Resolve: exact, else claude-<arg>, else unique substring.
534	    local cand; resolved=""
535	    for cand in "$base" "claude-$base" "$norm" "claude-$norm"; do
536	      if printf '%s\n' "$models" | command grep -qxF "$cand"; then
537	        resolved="$cand"
538	        break
539	      fi
540	    done
541	    if [ -z "$resolved" ]; then
542	      local hits count
543	      hits="$(printf '%s\n' "$models" | command grep -F "$norm" || true)"
544	      count="$(printf '%s\n' "$hits" | command grep -c . )"
545	      if [ "$count" = "1" ] && [ -n "$hits" ]; then
546	        resolved="$hits"
547	      else
548	        printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: '$arg' did not match a unique model. Try: copilot-model -l" >&2
549	        return 1
550	      fi
551	    fi
552	    resolved="$resolved$suffix"
553	  fi
554	
555	  local old; old="$(_copilot_model_current)"
556	  if [ "$old" = "$resolved" ]; then
557	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: already using $resolved (no change)"
558	    return 0
559	  fi
560	
561	  if [ "$target" = "local" ]; then
562	    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-model.XXXXXX")" || return 1
563	    if jq --arg m "$resolved" \
564	         '.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL = $m | .env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL = $m' \
565	         "$settings" >"$tmp"; then
566	      command mv -- "$tmp" "$settings"
567	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: $old -> $resolved  (project: $settings)"
568	      printf '%s\n' "  ⟳ restart Claude Code to apply (exit, then: claude -c)"
569	    else
570	      command rm -f -- "$tmp"
571	      printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: failed to update $settings" >&2
572	      return 1
573	    fi
574	  else
575	    command mkdir -p "$(command dirname "$statef")"
576	    printf '%s\n' "$resolved" >"$statef"
577	    printf '%s\n' "copilot-model: $old -> $resolved  (global: $statef)"
578	    printf '%s\n' "  applies to the next claude-copilot / copilot-run / copilot-here on"
579	  fi
580	}
581

636:## Copilot → Claude Code 代理 (proxy)
638:> 用 **GitHub Copilot** 訂閱裡的 Claude 模型來驅動 Claude Code，透過本機 [copilot-api](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api) 代理 (proxy)（經 `bunx` 執行，版本已釘選 (pinned)）。完整指南、**服務條款 (ToS) / 速率限制 (rate-limit) 風險** 與設定分層設計：[docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md](../tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md)。首次需執行 `copilot-proxy auth`（裝置登入 device login）。兩層啟用方式，都可隨時撤回，且都不碰會 commit 的 `./.claude/settings.json`（由 `claude-plans-here` 擁有）與 chezmoi 管理的 `~/.claude/settings.json`：`claude-copilot`（單一 session 環境變數、零檔案寫入）與 `copilot-here`（專案級、gitignored `settings.local.json`）。Claude Code 內建的 `/model` 選單會送出 Copilot 後端不接受的 Anthropic id —— 改用 `copilot-model` 釘選。
642:| `copilot-proxy [start\|stop\|restart\|status\|logs [N]\|whoami\|auth]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 管理 copilot-api 代理 (proxy)。`start` 在 `$COPILOT_PROXY_PORT`（預設 4141）背景啟動，帶 `--rate-limit $COPILOT_PROXY_RATE`（預設 15 秒）並等到能回應為止；`status` 顯示它提供的 Claude id；`whoami` 拿儲存的 token 對 GitHub 驗證並印出帳號/plan/quota（真正的登入檢查）；`auth` 執行一次性的裝置登入 (device login)（儲存 `ghu_` token）。環境變數：`COPILOT_PROXY_PORT`、`COPILOT_PROXY_RATE`、`COPILOT_API_PKG`（bunx 套件規格，預設 `copilot-api@0.7.0`） |
643:| `claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [args...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 一次性走代理的 Claude Code session，**零檔案寫入**：自動啟動代理，以 per-process 方式注入 `ANTHROPIC_*` 環境變數（shell 環境變數蓋過所有 settings 檔的 `env` 區塊）。有 specstory 時自動包成 `specstory run claude`（`--no-specstory` 退出）；額外參數透過 specstory 的 `-c` 傳給 claude。還原 = 下次直接跑 `claude` 即可 |
644:| `copilot-run <cmd...>` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 泛用積木：自動啟動代理，然後帶著代理 env 執行 *任意* 指令（例如 `copilot-run specstory run claude`、`copilot-run claude --resume`） |
645:| `copilot-here [on\|off\|status]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 專案級持續開關，透過 **gitignored** 的 `./.claude/settings.local.json`（覆蓋會 commit 的專案設定，所以 `plansDirectory` 完全不受影響）。`on` 用 jq 合併代理 env 區塊並確保 git 忽略該檔（`.git/info/exclude`）；`off` 只移除那些 key（保留其他內容，檔案清空才刪除）；`status` 顯示釘選狀態 + 模型，代理沒跑時警告。需要 `jq` |
646:| `copilot-model [<id>\|-l\|-c]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 切換釘選的 Copilot 模型（`ANTHROPIC_MODEL` + `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`）。`copilot-here` 開啟時寫 `./.claude/settings.local.json`，否則寫全域狀態檔 `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/model`（由 `claude-copilot`/`copilot-run` 讀取；`$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL` 可覆寫）。永遠不碰會 commit 的 `./.claude/settings.json`。支援模糊 id（`opus-4.8` → `claude-opus-4.8`），會對照即時的代理 `/v1/models` 驗證（代理未啟動時用靜態 Claude fallback 清單）；拒絕打錯字/不明確的輸入。無參數 → `fzf` 選單。`-l` 列出、`-c` 目前值 + 來源層。需要 `jq`。會印出重啟提醒（變更在啟動時才生效） |
```

3	# Pattern:

5	#     sentinel ~/.cache/chezmoi/last-apply after every chezmoi apply.
6	#   - At shell init (here) we record this shell session's birth time as a
7	#     temp marker file.
8	#   - On every prompt a precmd / PROMPT_COMMAND hook calls _chezmoi_reload_check.
9	#   - Check fires AT MOST ONCE per shell session, then short-circuits.
10	#
11	# This file is the single source of truth. The shell-specific hook registration
12	# (add-zsh-hook for zsh, blehook/PROMPT_COMMAND for bash) lives at the bottom,
13	# dispatched by $ZSH_VERSION/$BASH_VERSION at source time. We do NOT use
14	# dot_config/{zsh,bash}/*99_chezmoi_reload.{zsh,bash} because the bash side
15	# would run before this file (dot_bashrc.tmpl loads $BASH_CONFIG_DIR before
16	# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell to satisfy oh-my-bash's plugins=() prereq) and the
17	# backend function would not yet be defined.
18	#
19	# Opt out:
20	#   export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0    # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc or a per-shell secret file
21	#
22	# Cross-file maintenance: see CLAUDE.md "Cross-file maintenance rules" row.
23	
24	[[ "${CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT:-1}" = "0" ]] && return 0
25	
26	_CZ_RELOAD_SENTINEL="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/chezmoi/last-apply"
27	_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH="$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/.cz_birth.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || _CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH=""

29	_chezmoi_reload_cleanup() {
30	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" && -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] && rm -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH"
31	}
32	trap _chezmoi_reload_cleanup EXIT

34	# Resolve the *current* shell interpreter rather than $SHELL (which reflects
35	# /etc/passwd / chsh and can lag the real interpreter on first login).
36	_chezmoi_reload_current_shell() {
37	    if [[ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
38	        printf 'zsh'
39	    elif [[ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
40	        printf 'bash'
41	    else
42	        printf '%s' "$(basename "${SHELL:-sh}")"

50	    [[ -n "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" && -f "$_CZ_RELOAD_BIRTH" ]] || return 0

61	        c="$(tput setaf 6 2>/dev/null)"
62	        r="$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null)"
63	        printf '%sℹ%s chezmoi applied changes — run %sexec %s -l%s or %ssource %s%s to reload\n' \
64	            "$y" "$r" "$c" "$sh" "$r" "$c" "$rc" "$r"
65	    else
66	        printf 'i chezmoi applied changes - run `exec %s -l` or `source %s` to reload\n' \
67	            "$sh" "$rc"
68	    fi
69	}

71	# Proactive wrappers: run instead of `chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi update` when
72	# you want the new shell rc to take effect immediately. exec's a fresh login
73	# shell on success so PATH, completions, hooks, prompts all reinitialise.
74	cas() {
75	    chezmoi apply "$@" || return $?
76	    local sh
77	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
78	    exec "$sh" -l
79	}
80	cau() {
81	    chezmoi update "$@" || return $?
82	    local sh
83	    sh="$(_chezmoi_reload_current_shell)"
84	    exec "$sh" -l
85	}
86	
87	# czcfg - reconfigure dotfiles prompts on an already-initialized machine.
88	# Seeds the grouped TUI from your current chezmoi.toml values, then runs
89	# `chezmoi init --apply --prompt` (the SSOT wrapper, scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py)
90	# so changed answers actually take effect. `scripts/` isn't deployed, so we
91	# locate it via `chezmoi source-path`. Non-interactive single-key changes:
92	#   czcfg --set installLlmTools=true motdStyle=figlet --yes
93	# Does NOT exec a fresh shell itself — chezmoi apply's reload hint (above) does.
94	czcfg() {
95	    if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
96	        printf 'czcfg: uv not found; install it first (https://astral.sh/uv).\n' >&2
97	        return 1
98	    fi
99	    local src
100	    src="$(chezmoi source-path 2>/dev/null)" || {
101	        printf 'czcfg: could not resolve chezmoi source-path.\n' >&2
102	        return 1
103	    }
104	    uv run --script "${src}/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py" reconfigure "$@"
105	}
106	
107	# Hook registration — source-time dispatch by current shell. The other branch
108	# is never parsed at runtime, so zsh-only / bash-only syntax inside each
109	# branch is fine (but we keep both branches POSIX-clean anyway).
110	if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
111	    autoload -Uz add-zsh-hook 2>/dev/null
112	    add-zsh-hook precmd _chezmoi_reload_check
113	elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
114	    if [ -n "${BLE_VERSION:-}" ] && declare -f blehook >/dev/null 2>&1; then
115	        blehook PRECMD+=_chezmoi_reload_check
116	    else
117	        # Append without duplicating on re-source.
118	        case "${PROMPT_COMMAND:-}" in
119	            *_chezmoi_reload_check*) : ;;
120	            *) PROMPT_COMMAND="_chezmoi_reload_check${PROMPT_COMMAND:+;$PROMPT_COMMAND}" ;;
121	        esac
122	    fi
123	fi

63	# --- run-for: time-box any long-running / infinite command -----------------
64	# Run CMD for at most DURATION, then send SIGINT (same as Ctrl-C) so a script's
65	# `trap INT` summary still prints; escalate to SIGKILL after a grace if the
66	# command ignores the interrupt. Wraps GNU timeout — gtimeout on macOS, timeout
67	# on Linux (both shipped by the coreutils install in the devtools ansible role).
68	#
69	# Usage:  run-for DURATION CMD [ARGS...]
70	#   DURATION takes GNU timeout suffixes: 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d, or bare seconds.
71	#   RUN_FOR_SIGNAL      signal sent on expiry (default INT)
72	#   RUN_FOR_KILL_AFTER  grace before SIGKILL (default 5s)
73	# Exit status: 124 = the time-box was hit (command still running); otherwise
74	#   the command's own exit status passes through.
75	# Examples:
76	#   run-for 5m ping-monitor --gateway 10
77	#   run-for 30s ./some-infinite-loop.sh
78	run-for() {
79		[ "$#" -lt 2 ] && {
80			echo "Usage: run-for DURATION CMD [ARGS...]" >&2
81			return 2
82		}
83		local to dur
84		to="$(command -v gtimeout || command -v timeout)" || {
85			echo "run-for: GNU timeout not found (install coreutils)" >&2
86			return 127
87		}
88		dur="$1"
89		shift
90		"$to" --signal="${RUN_FOR_SIGNAL:-INT}" --kill-after="${RUN_FOR_KILL_AFTER:-5s}" "$dur" "$@"
91	}
92

94	# https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/frequently-asked-questions/design/#why-does-chezmoi-cd-spawn-a-shell-instead-of-just-changing-directory

145	#
146	# Writes reply (text) to stdout. Writes metadata line to stderr when

148	# Currently only Claude's JSON includes usage/cost — other agents just get a

150	_aiagent_invoke() {

152	  local json reply model_used tokens_in tokens_out cache_read cache_create cost duration rc
153	
154	  # Ensure spinner cleans up if the caller returns or we hit a trap.
155	  trap '_aicap_spinner_stop' EXIT INT TERM
156	
157	  case "$agent" in
158	    claude)
159	      # Conditional --model: empty AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL → claude picks its

167	        json=$(claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" --output-format json "$prompt")
168	        rc=$?

173	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.input_tokens // "?"')

177	        cost=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.total_cost_usd // "?"')
178	        duration=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.duration_ms // "?"')

The key tension I'm seeing: once `copilot-here on` pins the proxy settings via settings.local.json, calling `claude-copilot` (which uses `copilot-run` to inject env vars) becomes somewhat redundant since settings.local.json takes precedence anyway. But the real value of reusing `claude-copilot` is getting its specstory auto-detection logic for free, even though the env injection itself is now redundant-but-harmless. Both use the same default model source, so they're pointing to the same proxy—it's redundant but harmless. The user probably wants the specstory wrapping that `claude-copilot` provides, so calling it makes sense even if the env injection gets overridden by settings.local.json.

For cleanup, since `claude` catches SIGINT on Ctrl-C and the shell function continues to the next line, running `copilot-here off` sequentially after the command will work reliably.

I'm also thinking about whether to detect and preserve the prior state — if the user already had `copilot-here on` before running this, I shouldn't turn it off at the end. It's an edge case, but adding that check prevents accidentally unpinning their project and makes the function idempotent. The code overhead is minimal, so I'll include it.

## 1. Tab completion — NONE exists for any `copilot-*` function, and that is correct per repo convention

A broad grep for `copilot` across `dot_config/zsh/`, `dot_config/bash/`, and `dot_config/shell/` turned up the definitions only. The two other `dot_config/shell/` hits are unrelated model-id strings, not completions:

Every completion in the repo targets an `executable_*` CLI in `dot_dotfiles/bin/`, never a shell function. The registered targets:
- Bash (`dot_config/bash/*_completion.bash`): `complete -F` for `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`, `ping-monitor`, `dotcfg`, `agent-warmup`.
- Zsh (`dot_config/zsh/tools/*_completion.zsh`): `compdef` for `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`, `ping-monitor`, `dotcfg`, `agent-warmup` (plus `mi-router` self-gen in `47_mi_router.sh` and `worktrunk`/`wt`).

\```sh
# --- one-shot pinned session (Layer 2, auto-reverted) ---------------------------

# Combine copilot-here (settings.local.json pin — beats inherited env, see Gotchas)
# with claude-copilot's ephemerality: pin THIS project, run ONE specstory-wrapped
# session, then unpin — even on Ctrl-C / kill. The proxy must already be up (we only
# notify; start it with `copilot-proxy start`). If copilot-here is already ON here,
# the existing pin is left untouched on exit (safe to run inside a pinned project).
# Example:
#   claude-copilot-once                 # pin, run, auto-unpin
#   claude-copilot-once -c              # continue last session
#   claude-copilot-once --no-specstory  # raw claude, no markdown auto-save
claude-copilot-once() {
  case "${1:-}" in
    -h|--help)
      printf '%s\n' "Usage: claude-copilot-once [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
      printf '%s\n' "  Pin THIS project to the proxy (copilot-here on), run one Claude Code"
      printf '%s\n' "  session, then auto-unpin (copilot-here off) — even on Ctrl-C."
      printf '%s\n' "  Needs the proxy already running:  copilot-proxy start"
      return 0 ;;
  esac

  # 1. Proxy must already be answering — notify only, never auto-start.
  if ! _copilot_alive; then
    printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot-once: proxy not reachable on port $(_copilot_port)." >&2
    printf '%s\n' "  start it first:  copilot-proxy start" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  # copilot-here needs jq — fail early with a clear message.
  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot-once: jq is required (used by copilot-here)" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # 2. Don't clobber an existing pin: only turn OFF what we turn ON.
  local _cco_was_on=0
  if [ -f ".claude/settings.local.json" ] \
     && [ "$(jq -r '.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL // empty' ".claude/settings.local.json" 2>/dev/null)" != "" ]; then
    _cco_was_on=1
  fi

  if [ "$_cco_was_on" = "0" ]; then
    copilot-here on || return 1
    # Auto-unpin even on Ctrl-C / kill. Mirror tmux_status_run's INT/TERM/HUP
    # trap + explicit normal-path cleanup; a bare function-scope EXIT trap would
    # fire on the wrong event when bash sources this file (see explore notes).
    trap '_copilot_once_trap' INT TERM HUP
  else
    printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot-once: copilot-here already ON here — leaving the pin in place on exit."
  fi

  # 3. One session — specstory-wrapped + arg passthrough (reuses claude-copilot).
  claude-copilot "$@"
  local _rc=$?

  # 4. Revert only what we enabled.
  if [ "$_cco_was_on" = "0" ]; then
    trap - INT TERM HUP
    copilot-here off
  fi

  # 5. We never auto-stop the proxy — remind how.
  printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot-once: session ended. Proxy still running on $(_copilot_base)."
  printf '%s\n' "  stop it when done:  copilot-proxy stop"
  return $_rc
}

# Internal: INT/TERM/HUP handler — unpin, clear trap, re-raise INT so the
# interactive shell sees correct exit semantics (mirrors _tmux_status_run_trap
# in dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh).
_copilot_once_trap() {
  copilot-here off >/dev/null 2>&1
  trap - INT TERM HUP
  printf '\n%s\n' "claude-copilot-once: interrupted — unpinned (copilot-here off). Proxy still up." >&2
  kill -INT $$ 2>/dev/null
}
\```

Design notes / why this shape:
- **Notify-only on proxy-down** matches the user's step 1 ("說沒有則提示") — no auto-start.
- **Prior-state guard** (`_cco_was_on`) makes it idempotent: running it inside a project the
  user already pinned won't unpin them.
- **Trap = `INT TERM HUP` + explicit clear on the normal path**, mirroring the repo's one
  portable idiom (`tmux_status_run` @ `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh:167-193`). The trap
  is cleared on *every* path where it's set, so no leak in zsh (which doesn't make traps
  function-local by default). In practice a foreground Ctrl-C is caught by `claude` itself and
  cleanup runs via the normal path; the trap covers shell-level TERM/HUP.
- **No `emulate -L zsh` / `pipefail` block** (unlike `copilot-proxy`/`copilot-model`): this
  function has no failure-sensitive pipelines — only a `jq` command substitution. Keeping it
  out avoids needless surface. (If we prefer internal consistency, the lightweight
  `[ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh` guard is a safe add — flagging as optional.)

```text
1	# Copilot → Claude Code proxy
2	
3	Back [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) with the
4	**Claude models from a GitHub Copilot subscription**, via a local
5	reverse-engineered proxy — the maintained fork
6	[`caozhiyuan/copilot-api`](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api)
7	(npm `@jeffreycao/copilot-api`). The original
8	[`ericc-ch/copilot-api`](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api) is
9	officially unmaintained ([issue #233](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api/issues/233)
10	points at the fork) but still works via `COPILOT_API_PKG=copilot-api@0.7.0`.
11	Both packages share the same token file
12	(`~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`), so switching needs **no re-auth**.
13	
14	- **Shell helpers**: `~/.config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` (`copilot-proxy`, `claude-copilot`, `copilot-run`, `copilot-here`, `copilot-model`)
15	- **Runner**: `bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api` (pinned; matches the `bunx` convention in `07_bunx_cli.sh`)
16	- **Not installed by ansible** — pulled on demand via `bunx`, so it stays off the
17	  provisioning path.
18	
19	!!! warning "This violates GitHub Copilot's Terms of Service"
20	    Using a Copilot subscription to power a non-GitHub agent is not permitted, and
21	    copilot-api is reverse-engineered/unofficial. It can trigger GitHub's
22	    **abuse detection** and lead to **temporary suspension of Copilot access**.
23	    Claude Code is token-hungry (frequent background calls, large context) —
24	    note the fork has **no rate limiter** (see Gotchas); `COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1`
25	    reduces background chatter. Use at your own risk; prefer a personal account
26	    over a corporate seat.
27	
28	## Quick start
29	
30	```sh
31	copilot-proxy auth      # one-time: GitHub device login (stores a ghu_ token)
32	
33	claude-copilot          # one-off session on the proxy (auto-starts it; no file writes)
34	
35	copilot-here on         # OR: pin THIS project — plain `claude` uses the proxy
36	copilot-here off        # unpin — back to the real Anthropic backend
37	```
38	
39	## How it works
40
```
</details></tool-use>

81	
82	So the proxy uses the two layers nobody else owns:
83	
84	| Enable | Mechanism | Scope | Disable |
85	|---|---|---|---|
86	| `claude-copilot` / `copilot-run` | per-process env vars | one session | just run plain `claude` next time |
87	| `copilot-here on` | `./.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored) | this project, sticky | `copilot-here off` |
88	
89	```
90	~/.claude/settings.json          .claude/settings.json         shell env                    .claude/settings.local.json
91	(chezmoi: hooks/plugins)    <    (git: plansDirectory)     <   (claude-copilot)         <   (copilot-here on/off)
92	```
93	
94	(Shell env still beats the user- and project-level settings files, so
95	`claude-copilot` works everywhere `copilot-here` is off — it just cannot
96	*override* an active `copilot-here` pin.)
97	
98	## Shell helpers
99	
100	### `copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|logs [N]|whoami|auth]`
101	
102	Manages the background proxy on `$COPILOT_PROXY_PORT` (default `4141`).
103	
104	| Env var | Default | Meaning |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| `COPILOT_PROXY_PORT` | `4141` | port the proxy listens on |
107	| `COPILOT_API_PKG` | `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14` | `bunx` package spec (pin / upgrade; `copilot-api@0.7.0` = old original) |
108	| `COPILOT_PROXY_RATE` | `15` | `--rate-limit` seconds — **original package only** (the fork has no rate limiter) |
109	| `COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET` | `0` | `1` = inject extra quota-saving Claude Code env (see below); off by default because it slightly degrades the UX |
110	
111	Set these in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` (or the per-shell secrets files). `start` refuses
112	to run until `copilot-proxy auth` has stored a token, and waits up to ~20s for the
113	proxy to answer before returning. `start` detects the package flavor from
114	`COPILOT_API_PKG`: only the exact original `copilot-api` gets
115	`--rate-limit`/`--wait` (the fork's `start` doesn't have those flags).
116	
117	`copilot-proxy whoami` is the real login check: it prints your plan / quota
118	(fails loudly if the token is missing or expired). On the fork it queries the
119	running proxy's `/usage` endpoint (jq-summarized) and falls back to
120	`bunx <pkg> debug` when the proxy is down; on the original it runs
121	`check-usage`. Use it instead of eyeballing the token file — the token is a
122	plaintext credential and should not be opened in an editor.
123	
124	### `claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]` — one-off session
125	
126	Layer 1: run a single Claude Code session on the proxy with **zero file
127	writes**. Auto-starts the proxy if it isn't answering, then launches `claude`
128	with the `ANTHROPIC_*` env injected per-process (shell env beats the user- and
129	project-level settings files — but **not** an active `copilot-here` pin in
130	`settings.local.json`; see Gotchas).
131	
132	- Wraps in `specstory run claude` when specstory is installed (markdown
133	  auto-save — same convention as `scode`/`svibe`); opt out with
134	  `--no-specstory`. Extra args reach the claude CLI via specstory's
```

138	### `copilot-run <cmd...>` — generic env injector
139	
140	The building block under `claude-copilot`: auto-starts the proxy and runs *any*
141	command with the proxy env. Useful for other Anthropic-compatible tools or a
142	custom specstory invocation:

147	```

149	### `copilot-here [on|off|status]` — sticky per-project toggle
150	
151	Layer 2: pin **this project** to the proxy via `./.claude/settings.local.json`
152	so plain `claude` (and `scode`/`svibe` panes, which just run
153	`specstory run claude`) uses the proxy until you turn it off. Requires `jq`.
154	
155	- `on` — jq-merges the proxy `env` block into `settings.local.json` (creates it
156	  if missing) and makes sure git ignores the file (via `.git/info/exclude`;
157	  Claude Code only auto-gitignores files *it* creates). The committed
158	  `.claude/settings.json` (`plansDirectory` etc.) is never touched.
159	- `off` — removes exactly the env keys `on` added; other content you put in
160	  `settings.local.json` survives, and the file is deleted if it becomes empty.
161	- `status` — pinned? which base URL / model? warns when the proxy isn't running.

Summary — .claude/settings.local.json and gitignore

- Purpose: .claude/settings.local.json is the per-repository Local-scope settings file. Use it for personal overrides (machine- or user-specific settings) that you do not want committed or shared with the team.

- Automatic behavior: When Claude Code creates .claude/settings.local.json for you, it automatically configures Git to ignore that file (so it is added to .gitignore). If you create the file yourself, you must add it to .gitignore manually.

- Why use Local scope: Local overrides a project settings.json and is not shared via Git. Typical uses: testing configuration before committing, per-machine credentials or tweaks, personal preferences.

Important notes from the docs:
- Local location: .claude/settings.local.json (affects only you in this repo; not shared)
- Scopes precedence: Managed > Command-line args > Local > Project > User
- Claude Code will mark .claude/settings.local.json as gitignored when it creates it; if you add it manually, add an entry to .gitignore to prevent accidental commits.

Examples

1) Minimal .claude/settings.local.json example
{
  "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json",
  "env": {
    "MY_LOCAL_FLAG": "1"
  },
  "autoMemoryEnabled": false
}

2) Add to .gitignore (if creating file yourself)
# Ignore local Claude Code overrides
.claude/settings.local.json

3) Gitignore pattern to ignore all local/generated Claude files
# Claude Code local files
.claude/*.local.json
.claude/settings.local.json

If you want to verify gitignore changes, run:
- git status (to see if the file is tracked)
- git rm --cached .claude/settings.local.json (if you accidentally committed it previously) 

If you need an example for committing a project-level settings.json while keeping local overrides private:
- Commit .claude/settings.json (project-shared)
- Ensure .claude/settings.local.json is in .gitignore (local-only)

If you want, I can generate a ready-to-drop .gitignore snippet and a starter .claude/settings.local.json tuned for a specific purpose (e.g., disable auto memory, set local env vars, or temporary API-key helper). Which would you prefer?
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-03 06:38:29Z)**_

Done. Your instinct was right that the untracked `settings.local.json` needed handling — but the cleanest fix wasn't a new `.claude/.gitignore`; it was repairing the ignore mechanism `copilot-here` already had.

## What was wrong
`copilot-here on` already writes to `.git/info/exclude`, but with the pattern `.claude/settings.local.json`. Because that has an internal slash, git **anchors it to the repo root** — so your subdirectory project (`skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/.claude/…`) never matched, and the file showed as `??`. There was also a secondary bug: since `check-ignore` kept returning "not ignored" in subdirs, every `copilot-here on` appended another (still-useless) line.

## The fix
One line in `copilot-here on` — the pattern is now `**/.claude/settings.local.json` (un-anchored, matches at any depth). Verified end-to-end in a real repo with a subdir project:
- File created **and** ignored → `git status` clean (no more `??`).
- **Idempotent** → running `on` three times leaves exactly one exclude line.
- `copilot-here off` still removes the file cleanly.
- `bash -n` / `zsh -n` pass.

Since `claude-copilot-once` calls `copilot-here on`, it inherits this automatically.

## Why not `.claude/.gitignore` or root `.gitignore`
- **Root `.gitignore`** (what Claude Code itself uses) is a *committed* file — writing to it creates a diff you'd have to manage, and `copilot-here off` would then have to un-edit it. That breaks copilot-here's core promise of leaving nothing to commit.
- **`.claude/.gitignore`** works in subdirs but is a new working-tree file that itself needs committing or self-ignoring — more moving parts, and not Claude Code's convention.
- **`.git/info/exclude`** is per-clone and never committed, which is exactly the design intent here.

One note: this means the ignore is **local to your clone** (not shared with teammates). That's deliberate for a personal proxy toggle. If you'd instead prefer the file ignored for *everyone* who clones that project, say so and I'll switch `copilot-here` to append to the committed root `.gitignore` (Claude Code's convention) — but that changes the "zero committed artifacts" behavior, so I left it as the local exclude.

The docs I updated earlier still describe this accurately ("makes sure git ignores the file via `.git/info/exclude`"), so no further doc changes are needed.
